brief.scope: Independently assess GPT-6's inline lane-enforcement PLAN against owner requirements and current corrected authority docs. Find the smallest complete enforcement of today's dispatcher. Review implementable policy/work-spec/binding/refusal contracts, immutable profile versus existing machinery lane marker, instruction authority, protected writes/dependencies, resume/collect/land coverage and honest semantic/containment limits. No word blacklist or prompt-only enforcement claim. Reconcile ownership with the supplied consolidation review: task output requirements/adapter grants belong to the launch contract; lane policy consumes them without cyclic prerequisites or duplicate schemas. Doctrine corrections already landed here and remaining citations are separately adjudicated. Return <=1200-word verdict, essential corrections, concrete first contract/test/code scope and positive/negative acceptance. Read-only: no source/tests/settings/host/DB/network edits or vendor launches.

findings.where: 20260906T013410Z-plan-codex-670fff.json artifacts.PLAN, "One declarative owner" (LANE_POLICY_PATH in ops/lane.conf resolved through laneconf.py) and "Policy identity and source membership are protected configuration"; ops/conductor/tools/laneconf.py:138-140,170-189,193-197
findings.claim: The chosen owning home defeats the plan's own protection requirement. laneconf.conf_path() takes the whole configuration file from the environment (Path(os.environ.get("LANE_CONF", DEFAULT_CONF)), :140); values() overrides every declared key from the environment (:186-189); get() returns the environment value ahead of the file (:193-197). The only protection that exists, NAME_KEYS, guards the gitignored local file, not the environment, and does not cover a new key. So a policy path declared as LANE_POLICY_PATH is silently repointable by LANE_POLICY_PATH=... or LANE_CONF=... in the launcher's environment, which is exactly the 'ambient environment may not silently replace the policy authority' the plan promises. An enforcement boundary an environment variable can move is not enforcement.

artifacts.VERDICT:
VERDICT: changes. Independent read-only assessment of the PLAN carried inline at .dev/records/dispatches/20260906T013410Z-plan-codex-670fff.json (result.envelope.artifacts.PLAN), measured at HEAD 29f050971ee30a640ff5c367a6af2bb892e6bc81 against base c06ed9442ba51c9e96aa8de9f9bde93d0843a6cc. No implementation approved, nothing dispatched, no file written.

ADMITTED AS CORRECT. The plan obeys every owner constraint I can check. No word ban: it enforces through files, dependencies and declared sources, and says outright that no prompt or classifier proves semantic meaning. No enforcement overclaim: it separates prescribed, implemented and live behaviour, refuses to certify cross-harness interception, and leaves conductor-enforce.py unarmed. Forbidden operations refuse rather than ask for owner approval. The immutable-binding design is right and compatible: record.py forces the top-level lane marker (record.py:25,79) as infrastructure identity, and the plan keeps it while nesting the work-profile binding under brief.policy — which validate() tolerates today, so legacy records still validate and acquire no guessed profile. It refuses on flag/spec disagreement instead of picking a winner, keeps role, stage and harness as separate dimensions, and names the acceptance holes correctly: write resume bypasses settlement (launch.py:1855-1857) and collect exports its own dispatch ref (launch.py:1943), so both need the check. Its refusal classes are on the docs/wire.md wire.

WHERE IT FAILS. Five corrections are essential; the findings carry the evidence.

1. The owning home defeats the protection (p1). LANE_POLICY_PATH resolved through laneconf is environment-overridable at both levels (laneconf.py:140 LANE_CONF, :186-189 per-key, :193-197 get), and NAME_KEYS guards only the local file. Put the policy at a fixed tracked path resolved from the repository root, as DEFAULT_CONF already does, and drop the configuration key. That also removes the closure obligation in correction 5.

2. Ownership with the launch track (p2). Declared job outputs and per-harness adapter grants belong to the launch/task contract, replacing the job-name branch at launch.py:952,959,1189,1213. Lane policy consumes them as one term of the permitted-write intersection and falls back to profile roots when a job declares none. Drop E5. Neither track becomes the other's prerequisite; the interface is one field in jobs.json, read if present.

3. D1-D3 are stale (p2). They were measured at 83ee5c6, before 7e07a13 and 1552699 landed. Re-base onto the residue, which is separately adjudicated; do not re-dispatch the same file list.

4. Size and effect (p2). Twenty-one buckets, and under the plan's own ordering nothing is refused until E15. Cut to the five below.

5. Floor blast radius (p2). laneconf closure and literals are pinned against the real tree by test_laneconf and run by suites.sh. literals already forbids the "dev" token in lane code — it is the existing mechanical form of 'profile names are configuration data'. Extend that instrument's exemption table deliberately rather than re-proving the rule in new tests only.

SMALLEST COMPLETE ENFORCEMENT OF TODAY'S DISPATCHER. Five buckets, each one to three files, in this order.

A1 contract and data. C writes ops/conductor/lane-policy.md and ops/lane-policy.json: profile ids as mapping keys, permitted write roots, forbidden dependency roots, protected authority paths, and the refusal table (lane-profile, lane-policy, lane-write, lane-dependency, lane-resume). It states plainly that for claude and grok this is detection at acceptance, not prevention in the harness, because containment is policy-only there (launch.py:379-381; CLAUDE_DENIED_TOOLS is WebFetch, WebSearch, Agent, Task).

A2 evaluator. I writes ops/conductor/tools/lane_policy.py: pure, stdlib, repo-root resolution, no CLI, no conventions docstring, decide(profile, paths) and depends(entrypoints). launch.py already loads a conductor tool this way (launch.py:62), so the edge exists.

A3 binding. --profile on launch.py, passed through dispatch.sh and go.sh, captured with the policy digest under brief.policy; record.py validates its shape when present. Unknown, missing or conflicting selection refuses exit 2 with one expected-found-needed line before the snapshot is minted. Scope text, inputs, envelope and environment cannot reclassify.

A4 acceptance at the seams that exist. One _lane_check() called from three sites: in _settle before the write-role fetch at launch.py:1687, in the write-resume branch at :1857, and in _collect before its export at :1943. It consumes the entries settlement already measures (_residual_entries, changed) rather than a second enumeration. A violation invalidates the envelope through _invalidate_envelope, no dispatch ref is exported, and the evidence is preserved.

A5 dependency closure. A floor test asserting the dev entrypoint closure imports nothing under vendor/, src/, packages/ or bin/console, run with no application tree present. Documentation references and fixture apparatus (ops/devlane/fixtures/tests/test_symfony_app_app.py) stay clean.

Deferred until a measured obligation: instruction-source digest pinning at onboarding, jobs.json capability rows, hook projection, doctor, ladder and land consumers, MCP projection. For doctrine regression prefer the structural assertion e5ec77 performed by hand — the boundary section exists at its anchor, its links resolve, the onboarding reading list reaches it — over digests on frequently edited prose, which will be re-stamped as routine and prove change, never meaning.

POSITIVE ACCEPTANCE. P1 a dev change under ops/ that reads shared contracts and describes Symfony passes. P2 the same writes under a prod profile pass, including a Composer manifest change, and refuse under dev. P3 a third synthetic profile with its own roots behaves identically after adding configuration data only, consumers unchanged. P4 a legacy record with no brief.policy still validates, reads and reports unbound.

NEGATIVE ACCEPTANCE. N1 missing, unknown, duplicate or conflicting profile refuses before any fake child starts. N2 scope prose, quoted history, environment and a resume prompt cannot move the captured profile; with the fixed policy path, LANE_CONF and a stray environment key cannot move the policy. N3 a dev write to vendor/, src/, packages/ or composer.json refuses at settlement and no refs/dispatch ref appears. N4 renames across roots, symlink escape, prefix neighbours and untracked or ignored product writes are caught, while the enumerated cache shapes still pass. N5 status ok, verdict approve, exit 0 and a successful collection verification do not override a violation. N6 a dev entrypoint importing vendor/autoload.php or booting bin/console fails A5 while a prose reference passes. R1 a stationary binding resumes and revalidates. R2 changed policy bytes, profile or template refuse before attempt markers move and prior terminal evidence stays byte-identical. R3 resumed write and collected work meet the same check as fresh work.

artifacts.limits: Read-only review of a plan, not of an implementation: every claim about the proposed design is read from the PLAN string in the supplied record, and every claim about current behaviour is read from source at this ref. I ran no suite — the floor is inventoried, not certified green here — and executed neither onboard.py, laneconf closure/literals, nor the launcher, so the closure and literals consequences are derived from reading the checker and its pinned tests, not from a red run I produced. Absence claims are 'looked and found nothing' by the named commands over the tracked tree; they say nothing about untracked files, live sessions or operator homes. The doctrine residue at MCP-RESEARCH-2026-09-05.md:130 and .dev/wip/overview.md:490-496 is reported only as context for re-basing D1-D3; it is under separate adjudication and I did not re-litigate it. I did not review the sibling consolidation PLAN itself, only the reconciliation obligations its supplied review (b0e12f) creates for this one. The five-bucket path A1-A5 is a recommendation for conductor comparison, not an admitted contract; no producer identity is bound and no implementation is approved.
